blocks.s: Regarding knowledge, Augustine distinguishes matutinal, meridional, and vespertinal knowledge. Matutinal knowledge is the knowledge of things as they exist in the Word of God — that is, the knowledge of creatures as they are in their eternal exemplars and ideas in the divine intellect, a knowledge clearer and more perfect than any other creaturely knowledge. Meridional knowledge is the beatific vision of God himself, face to face, which is the knowledge of noon when the light is highest and no shadow remains — this is the knowledge of the blessed in the homeland. Vespertinal knowledge is the knowledge of things as they exist in their own proper nature, which is a dimmer and lower form of knowing, since creatures known in themselves are known in an inferior mode compared with their eternal exemplars.
